source_message.text:
You’re hired, Nikhil—congratulations. This was a strong first set: you were the only clipper to finish before the deadline, and the quality supported that result. Your moment capturing was on point, and the font selection worked well.

Two small changes should guide your work going forward. One clip was too short, so remember that clips must remain within 20-120 seconds to deliver the complete message or goal. Also, the captions and letters did not use color; adding it will make them stand out more and should improve watch time.

These are not major problems, only points of polish. Overall, your first set was strong enough to secure the position.

Payment for these clips will arrive on Thursday. After that, you’ll be properly onboarded through a better guideline video explaining exactly how we create clips, the do’s and don’ts, and what is expected.

There is also a larger responsibility ahead: you will serve as the lead clipper for a pod of 12 clippers while continuing to produce your own clips. In addition, you’ll approve work from the other 11, keep the pod operating smoothly, and make sure everyone meets the standard. Before the role begins, I’ll walk you through how all of that will work.

Congratulations again—we’ll talk soon.

Start by reading the complete clipper guidelines here: <https://notes.emberframe.example/p/Video-Editing-Standards-7316>

Nothing inside should be skipped. Watch the introduction video, the good clip examples, the bad clip examples, and the brand guidelines; this is the most important step.

After reviewing everything, create 8 clips from one video on the YouTube channel. Every clip must meet these requirements:
\- It captures a complete moment from beginning to end, not a fragment
\- It teaches something or provides a real lesson
\- It uses clean, professional editing that follows the examples, with no crazy effects or transitions and only simple, quality work

Passing this trial means I will hire you immediately on a flat $700-900 per month retainer for 180 approved clips per month. In addition, I will personally train you to become a Lead Clipper who manages a team and can earn up to $4,500 per month.

I genuinely want this to work, so take your time reviewing the guidelines and every example before sending me 8 perfect clips.

3\. **Correct the fonts** — return to the brand guidelines and use the exact specified font instead of guessing.

Nikhil, you are halfway there. I’m offering you this chance because I believe you can do it, but your next submission has to be perfect. Work through the full guidelines and redo all 8 clips.

I’m rooting for you, so show me what you can do.

Darius

Hey,

I'll start with the big picture: only 6 clippers have been hired right now, and you're one of them. You're joining from the very beginning, which gives you a real opportunity to grow with this from day one.

Tomorrow, I'll send everything you need: the full training material, the guidelines, and your assigned Instagram account.

Here are the details you asked about, starting with compensation and output:

**Payment, approval, and monthly target:**
For producing 140 approved clips, the retainer is $700-900 per month. The target works out to roughly 4-5 clips per day, and maintaining consistent daily output is what will keep you on track. I personally review and approve every clip, and a clip counts toward the 140 only after I approve it. You can also earn performance bonuses based on how the clips perform on Instagram, with as much as $800 available for a single clip that blows up. That puts your earning potential well above the flat fee.

**Source videos and deliverables:**
You'll work with Arden Vale's long-form YouTube videos. Your job is to watch them, identify complete moments—a full lesson, a story, or a real point—and shape each one into a standalone 70-85 second clip for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.

That's the full setup. Get ready, and let's crush this.

Darius

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Brother,

Plan around the timing first: **DEADLINE: Thursday.** Every clip must reach me by Thursday morning—not Thursday night—because I have to review and approve all of them before they go live Friday. Anything I do not have by then does not get posted this week.

The big update is that you now have access to the B-roll footage, which can take your clips to the next level.

B-roll link: <https://emberframe.example/drive/folders/campaign-assets-4827>

Using this B-roll footage alongside Arden's long-form YouTube videos, create **12 perfect clips**. Every clip must follow these rules exactly:

- Run 70 to 85 seconds minimum
- Capture a complete moment, with the full lesson or story presented from start to finish
- Integrate B-roll naturally in support of the message, never as random footage
- Use white text only, with no colored fonts or text effects
- Keep the editing clean and simple, without heavy animations or flashy transitions
- Keep background music at low volume and never louder than Arden's voice
- Make each clip standalone so that even someone unfamiliar with Arden can watch it and understand it completely

Move fast. To strengthen each moment rather than merely fill space, use the B-roll only where it adds power to the message.

Submit your 12 clips as a Google Drive folder link, use your name for the folder title, and set the folder so anyone with the link can view it.

Because these are the first real clips going live, make every one perfect.

Darius
